question: Will ISRO launch the GSLV-F18 / NVS-03 (IRNSS-1L) mission on October 15 or 16, 2026?

calls.reasoning: ISRO sources (via Times of India, relayed by spacedaily/corsstations/MSN) target a 15-20 Oct 2026 window with preference for the early end; campaign began 14 Sep, first stage stacked ~21 Sep, satellite at SHAR since August. As of 5 Oct no official ISRO date; trackers disagree (Wikipedia list: Oct TBD 17:00 UTC; NextSpaceflight: NET Oct; RocketLaunch.Live: Oct 13; SpaceRealm: Oct 31 TBD). Recent GSLV Mk II flights (F12, F14, F15) launched on the publicly set date, but F16/NISAR slipped ~6 weeks from its NOTAM window. Hitting a specific 2-day slice of a 6-day working window, with no date fixed 10 days out, skews toward a slip. No human prediction market found (harness found none on Polymarket/Manifold; I did not search Kalshi or bookmakers separately).

calls.reasoning: Reference class: ISRO GSLV Mk II launches. Once ISRO officially announces a date, it usually holds, with slips of 0-2 days (NVS-01, F14/INSAT-3DS, NVS-02, NISAR). Here, 10 days out, there is no official notice. Late-September press citing ISRO sources (Times of India via SpaceDaily, Asianet, The Week, DT Next) gives a working target of 15-20 Oct, preferring the early end, with 'all efforts' on 15 Oct. RocketLaunch.org notes the listing reverted to 'NET October TBD' after NOTAMs were cancelled; that suggests an earlier ~13 Oct slot (still shown on NextSpaceflight search snippets) was dropped. The 2-day YES window sits at the front of a 6-day target window and leaves no room for further slips. GSLV also has a history of multi-month delays. Weighing these, I land a bit under 40%. Market check: Polymarket, Manifold and Kalshi searches found no market.

calls.reasoning: Reference class: unofficial GSLV launch targets reported by media about 10 days out with no ISRO notice; Run 2's rough base-rate note says such targets slip more often than announced dates (uncounted). Here the satellite is ready, stage 1 was stacked 21 Sep, and the reported focus is Oct 15. But there is still no official notice, NOTAMs for about Oct 13/15 were cancelled, a 31-day campaign would be fast for GSLV, and the YES window is only the first 2 days of a 15-20 Oct target, so any further slip resolves NO. calls.reconciliation: Disputes: (1) whether ISRO has issued an official date or time; (2) whether a NOTAM covers Oct 15/16; (3) whether an Oct 13 slot is still live; (4) how likely an internal target is to hold. I ran three targeted searches (launch date; NOTAM for Oct 15; news this week). They found only the late-Sep reporting of the 15-20 Oct target with focus on Oct 15. There was no official ISRO notice, no NOTAM text, and no news dated Oct 1-5. A search summary repeated the tracker's Oct 13 entry, which is stale and would resolve NO anyway. So the factual picture matches the dossiers: no confirmation 10 days out, and NOTAMs previously cancelled. The rest is judgment. The fast ~31-day campaign, the earlier Sep->Oct slip, the NOTAM withdrawal and the narrow 2-day front-edge window outweigh satellite readiness and NavIC urgency. I bet the lower half of the run range, carrying a reference class similar to Run 3's.
